title: The Legibility Constraint
excerpt: The most interesting thing about India’s new retail algorithmic-trading framework is something it does not do. It does not ban black boxes.

title: Compression Staleness
excerpt: Groww published a useful explainer last week on the AAA-to-D bond-rating scale: AAA at one end, default at the other, with a series of increasingly risky grades in between. It is exactly the kind of simplification retail investing needs.

title: You Can Buy Expertise. Can You Buy Elapsed Time?
excerpt: S&P Global agreed this month to acquire OpenZeppelin, one of the best-known names in smart-contract security. title: The Unwritten Approval Layer
excerpt: In late May, Binance appeared close to securing the European licence it had been pursuing through Greece. Greek officials had reportedly told the company its MiCA application was complete; Binance had prepared an announcement, and its CEO was planning a trip to Athens.

title: Three Ways to Buy a Capability You Don
excerpt: On September 18, Japan’s SBI Group invested in Singapore-based dtcpay as part of its $25 million Series A. dtcpay already offers what SBI wants: Regulated infrastructure that moves between stablecoins and traditional payments, supported by licences across multiple markets.

title: What Aged Cheese and Long-Duration Bonds Have in Common
excerpt: A wheel of cheese can age for two years. A government bond can lock up capital for thirty years.

title: A good environment can become almost indistinguishable from skill when all you see is the final outcome
excerpt: Wine has a useful way of exposing a problem that exists far beyond wine. Roman Weil once tested whether people could distinguish wines from highly rated vintages from those produced in supposedly weaker years.

title: The Rest Day Is Where the Training Actually Happens
excerpt: The workout doesn’t make you stronger. It creates the reason your body has to become stronger.

title: The Cost of Being Right Too Early
excerpt: Being wrong gets most of the attention in forecasting. We dissect bad assumptions, bad theses and bad decisions.
thesis: Being right and being wrong cost the same P&L if your timing is off.

title: The Attribution Problem Hiding Inside Every Team Win
excerpt: Ten thousand AI agents reportedly worked together on a proposed solution to one of mathematics' hardest open problems: The Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem. Understanding the problem matters before getting to the AI.
thesis: Ten thousand AI agents solved a hard problem together. Who gets the credit?

title: Ethereum's 2029 Deadline Is a Training Taper With No Fixed Race Day
excerpt: Ethereum does not really have a quantum-computing deadline in the way most headlines make it sound. It has a planning target, and the distinction matters.
thesis: Ethereum's 2029 deadline isn't a deadline. It's a training taper with no fixed race day.

title: Stablecoins Just Ran Into One of Finance's Oldest Problems
excerpt: Singapore's central bank proposed a new set of stablecoin rules this month. Issuers would need to maintain reserves of at least 100%, keep those assets appropriately segregated, and — this is the part worth sitting with — would not be allowed to offer holders interest or other benefits simply for holding.
thesis: Stablecoin reserves are getting stricter. Interest on holdings is the line regulators won't cross.

title: The Perimeter Follows the Customer
excerpt: On September 9, India's Financial Intelligence Unit issued non-compliance notices to 15 crypto platforms. It also sought takedowns of their apps and URLs in India.
thesis: Fifteen crypto platforms got non-compliance notices. The perimeter moved to where the customer is.

title: UPI Just Became More Like a Crypto Wallet Than Anyone Announced
excerpt: From September 4, UPI stopped showing your full phone number to the person you're paying. Only the last four digits are visible in places where the mobile number previously appeared.
thesis: UPI stopped showing your full phone number. Payments are quietly becoming more like wallets.

title: The Auction Built to Stop Manipulation Got Manipulated First
excerpt: When India's Closing Auction Session went live in August, I wrote about it before Per Diem existed as a newsletter. The first few sessions looked strange.
thesis: The auction built to stop manipulation got manipulated first.

title: 21 Competing Banks Just Agreed on What Not to Compete Over
excerpt: Twenty-one banks just agreed to build something together. Not compete over.
thesis: Twenty-one competing banks just agreed on what not to compete over.

title: Your Portfolio Doesn't Rebalance on Every Tick. Why Does Your Attention?
excerpt: A 60/40 portfolio doesn't rebalance at 60.3/39.7. It waits. It moves only when the drift becomes large enough to matter.
thesis: Your portfolio doesn't rebalance on every tick. Why does your attention?

title: Anthropic Built a KYC Tier for AI, Not a Product Tier
excerpt: On September 1, Anthropic shipped two models: Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1. Same underlying model. Different safeguards.
thesis: Anthropic shipped two identical models with different safeguards — a KYC tier, not a product tier.

title: Zerodha and Groww Just Made Opposite Bets on Where the Margin Actually Lives
excerpt: On September 1, Zerodha's advisory arm got SEBI approval to operate as a merchant banker. Not a headline event — but it landed two months after Nithin Kamath went after Groww in public for almost the opposite move.
thesis: Zerodha and Groww just made opposite bets on where the margin actually lives.

title: Your Stop-Loss and Your Taper Are the Same Idea
excerpt: A stop-loss in trading and a pacing plan in endurance sport look like completely different things. One protects capital. The other protects your body.
thesis: A stop-loss in trading and a pacing plan in endurance sport protect the same thing, differently.
